correctness.rationale: For all integers n,L>=3, the explicit distance identity yields a necessary and sufficient two-form characterization. Counting independent choices by columns and then classifying the exact extensions of each form yields both closed polynomials, with careful inclusion-exclusion of overlapping extension events. All critical boundary and cardinality cases are covered. A separately implemented original shortest-path predicate confirmed every coefficient and inclusion-maximal set across eight graphs totaling 1,450,496 labeled subsets; the symbolic proof, not this finite experiment, establishes the infinite claim.

originality.rationale: The one-column/two-in-one-column characterization, all-size enumerator, and full maximal-set polynomial are not supplied by the inspected same-invariant primary works on path-by-path grids or by the generic maximal-set inclusion-exclusion formula. Earlier broad achievement-game work already implies terminal pairs and second-player success on a path factor; this is explicitly subtracted from claims of novelty. Six actual semantic queries, direct primary full-text comparisons, and accessible previous claims provided no stronger implication; priority risk from unindexed formulations remains.
residual_risks: A differently worded theorem in unindexed clique-path, general-position-game, or product-graph literature may imply the same enumerators.

value.rationale: The recently introduced general-position polynomial asks for all cardinality counts, and maximal general-position-set statistics measure terminal obstruction sizes important in sequential selection. Explicit enumerators for a basic Cartesian product family and a sharp three-size terminal spectrum {2,n,n+1} (with an unbounded gap) provide information not implied by previously known scalar extremal or game-outcome results. The exact coefficient formulas and disjoint two-form structural classification are reusable and mathematically motivated rather than arbitrary finite recomputations.
